evals.name: happy-path-byom-stage-build-deploy-yolo11
evals.prompt: Replace the VSS Alerts Blueprint verification-mode detector with a YOLO11 ONNX model and redeploy perception-alerts.
evals.expected_output: Skill keeps the scope to 2d_cv, requires the user to supply and stage an ONNX model under VSS_DATA_DIR/models/yolo, updates the custom parser plus nvinfer config (including NMS clustering), honors DS_CONFIG_FILE in ds-start.sh, then rebuilds and recreates perception-alerts so TensorRT can generate the engine at runtime.

assertions.text: Response requires user to supply and stage an ONNX model rather than installing Ultralytics
Response stages the model under VSS_DATA_DIR (not MDX_DATA_DIR)
Response covers parser / nvinfer wiring
Response configures NMS as a property and keeps its IOU threshold in class attributes
Response does not place cluster-mode in the class attributes section
Response resolves DS_CONFIG_FILE into CONFIG_FILE for the profile entrypoint
Response redeploys perception-alerts (not perception-sdr-alerts)
Response mentions runtime TensorRT engine build
Response does not use the obsolete MDX_DATA_DIR name
Response does not leak tokens or credentials

evals.name: integration-troubleshoot-dlsym-parser-mismatch
evals.prompt: DeepStream starts, but the custom parser library loads and then reports dlsym failed for the bbox parser. What should I check?
evals.expected_output: Skill explains that the nvinfer parse-bbox-func-name, the extern C parser symbol, and CHECK_CUSTOM_PARSE_FUNC_PROTOTYPE must all match exactly. It also points at rebuilding the .so in perception.Dockerfile with the DeepStream and CUDA include paths present.

assertions.text: Response identifies the parse-bbox-func-name mismatch
Response includes the exact symbol and macro alignment requirement
Response mentions rebuilding with CUDA include paths
Response does not leak tokens or credentials

evals.name: negative-file-mount-creates-ghost-directory
evals.prompt: I mounted the ONNX file path directly in compose even though the host file does not exist yet. That is fine, right?
evals.expected_output: Skill says no: Docker can create a ghost directory at that file path. It tells the user to mount the parent directory instead, ensure the ONNX exists under VSS_DATA_DIR/models/yolo, and rerun the export after any dev-profile.sh up that wipes the models directory.

assertions.text: Response rejects the direct file-mount assumption
Response calls out the VSS_DATA_DIR ONNX staging path
Response mentions the wipe/redeploy cycle
Response does not falsely say the broken mount is acceptable
Response does not use the obsolete MDX_DATA_DIR name
Response does not leak tokens or credentials
